title: Fixed cell noise statistics permit a 22 to 27 percent sum-variance gap in eight worm site models
abstract: We tested whether static population covariance and full single-cell autocovariance fix temporally averaged population noise in models of eight worm brain maps. Independent Gaussian site noises had fast and slow components with time constants of 1 and 10. We fixed every site variance and every target slow-noise share. A linear program gave sharp bounds for the variance of the target sum averaged over a window of 10. Maximum variance was 1.217 to 1.269 times minimum variance, while the instantaneous joint law and each target marginal process were identical. Fixing an added slow-noise budget for each source reduced the ratios to 1.066 to 1.104. We give a row-space test for identification and numerical checks. This is a conditional model result, not measured neural noise. Unknown gains, release laws, partial maps and no linked activity data limit biological use. Code, aggregate results, a figure, hashes and external retrieval instructions support reproduction.

display.caption: Sharp sum-noise variance bounds with fixed anatomy, static covariance, and full target autocovariance. Time constants and window are model assumptions. Lines are bounds, not animal confidence intervals.
